Observations:  
- Channel 3 has high L2 weights only on the outer ring (row 0, row 9, column 0, column 9), e.g. row 0 values 0.64â0.75, row 9 values 0.51â0.69, while inner cells are ~0.25â0.47. This is clearly the fixed wall/border channel.  
- Channel 0 has large weights only in row 8, columns 1â8: e.g. (r8,c1)=8.24, (r8,c8)=9.73, while all other rows are ~0.3â0.4. This indicates a controllable object constrained to the bottom row â a paddle.  
- Channel 2 has high weights in the top rows 1â3: e.g. (r3,c1)=6.06, (r3,c7)=6.20, (r1,c5)=2.94. This suggests static objects at the top â bricks.  
- Channels 1 and 4 have high weights across the playable area, especially lower rows: ch4 max 19.87 at (r7,c4), ch1 max 17.41 at (r4,c3). These are consistent with a moving ball and an empty/background channel.  
- Output layer: W3 has very large positive weights for action 3 (left) and action 4 (right), e.g. row 11 col 3 = 4.057, row 24 col 4 = 3.031, row 22 col 3 = -5.336. Up/down (actions 1,2) have weights similar to no-op, so only left/right are meaningfully used. b3 is roughly flat: [1.221, 1.008, 1.024, 0.897, 1.298].  
- Top W1 connections show hidden units combining ch1/ch4 in lower rows with ch0 at row 8 and ch2 at top rows, exactly as needed to track a ball near the paddle and aim at bricks.

Reasoning:  
Games where the controlled object can move anywhere on the grid (Sokoban, Snake, Frogger, Maze) are ruled out because channel 0 is strongly active only on row 8. Pong is ruled out because the paddle is not on a side column. Space Invaders is ruled out because there is no fire action; up/down are not used, while left/right dominate. A bottom-row paddle, top-row static bricks, a moving ball, and only left/right mattering fit Breakout perfectly.

Game:  
Breakout (Atari Breakout / Brick Breaker).

Description:  
The agent moves a paddle left and right along the bottom row to bounce a ball upward and destroy bricks arranged at the top; reward is given for breaking bricks.

Confidence:  
92%
